From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, SooJin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Interview slate & leveling questions for Evan Park (Sr. Inference Eng)

Thanks Marissa — I skimmed the slate. A couple of role clarifications:

1) Primary focus for the hire is serving runtime (productionization, latency SLOs, batching). Secondary is model integration patterns (token caching, KV cache ops). We should de-emphasize lower-level transformer architecture theory unless candidate raises it.

2) Leveling: for Sr we expect ownership of service-level design decisions, clear tradeoffs on latency/cost, and ability to scope optimizations end-to-end (not just kernel-level). Please make that explicit in the readout page under "impact examples".

3) Interview timebox: keep runtime deep-dive to 45m with a 10m follow-up. Add one prompt on cross-team communication/incident response (behavioral).

I'll annotate the attached PDF and send back suggestions.

—Grace
Grace O'Connor | Hiring Manager, Serving Runtime

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, SooJin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 12:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Interview slate & leveling questions for Evan Park (Sr. Inference Eng)

Agree with Grace. Two bar-raiser anchors I'd add to the eval-anchors doc:

- System decomposition: candidate must identify at least two independent failure modes for a real-time serving stack and propose mitigations (e.g., KV-cache invalidation, hot-shard throttling, model-variant fallback).

- Tradeoff articulation: present a short matrix comparing 3 scaling approaches (horizontal pooling, model quantization, dynamic seq-len truncation) with cost/latency/quality bullets.

I'll edit the PDF and drop the version in Drive. Also recommend we ask candidates to whiteboard a short canary/rollback plan for a config change that reduces batch size (safety/observability focus).

Markus
Markus Klein | Bar-Raiser — Inference Systems

From: SooJin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Interview slate & leveling questions for Evan Park (Sr. Inference Eng)

Thanks — I reviewed the annotated anchors. A few operational notes for debrief:

- Scoring: use the 1-4 rubric in the PDF but require a pass on both "system thinking" and "delivery/ownership" for hire. If someone scores a 1 on either, flag as block.
- Evidence: ask interviewers to provide one concrete example from the candidate for each anchor rather than high-level impressions.
- Timing: I'll run the debrief 30m after the last interview to capture fresh notes.

Also adding: if the panel is split (2-2), preference is to ask for a follow-up take (asynchronous written question) before rejecting.

I'll update the debrief slide and share before the onsites.

—Soojin
Soojin Lee | Recruiting Ops (on hiring coordination)
